rationale: Stable source fixes max_candidates=256 and blocks new candidate creation at capacity after an immature-only stale prune; default mature candidates have no reclamation path.
Stable supported docs do not define max_candidates as a lifetime mature-memory cap, active working-set budget, or cache, and do not explicitly make mature candidates permanent.

The v0.5 Master Plan mentions Assembly stability/decay plus candidate decay and candidate budget as anti-proliferation design language, but it does not specify that mature candidates must be reclaimed; the existing immature-prune path is therefore not contradicted by an explicit mature-lifecycle contract.

Supported/default callers do not override max_candidates=256. The retained protocol has bounded learning horizons (48 training episodes per seed; 24 for plasticity ablation) and held-out evaluation does not learn Assemblies.
No supported test/caller promises continued acquisition of novel patterns after capacity saturation, and no supported default test deliberately reaches saturation.

Static source also does not prove saturation impossible within the bounded horizon because one episode may yield multiple candidate patterns. Saturation is therefore unestablished rather than structurally unreachable.
Checkpoint serialization preserves candidate state but stable docs/source do not elevate persistence mechanics into a lifetime lifecycle contract.
